caption: Figure 43-1
The Character wheel, left, and the Here and now wheel.

blocks.p: With no window holding the controller, a tap on each direction of the D-pad opens a wheel of actions; Table 43-1 lists the four. The left stick keeps walking while a wheel is open. To take an action from a wheel:

list: Tap a direction of the D-pad. Its wheel opens.
Point at a slice with the right stick.
Let go of the right stick. The slice you pointed at runs.

blocks.note: The same direction or *B* closes a wheel. A slice put on a chord runs without opening its wheel. Chapter 44 describes the chords.

marks.text: LB + A eats without opening the wheel. A slice on a chord shows it.
Under the pointer: the slice's name, its chord and what it does.

blocks.p: A slice with a mark in its corner holds a wheel of its own. Let go of the right stick on it and the ring changes in place to the inner wheel, which stays open: there the right stick points, letting go takes and *B* backs out one level. The line under the ring names where you are, such as *Character + Use*. A slice that cannot be done now stays in its place, stippled, and its bubble gives the reason.

caption: Figure 43-2
Inside the Use slice, with Smoke pointed at. Below it, a window's help line.

blocks.p: While a window has the controller, the help line at its foot names what each button does there, beside a picture of the button. The pictures are drawn for the controller you use.

marks.text: A slice that can't be done now says why.
The footer names what each button does here. The pictures are drawn for your controller.

sticky.text: Point with the right stick, let go to take.
